# Third-party skills

Skills written by other people that I use but don't own. Nothing here is forked, copied, or vendored: [`skills.json`](./skills.json) is a curated list of *which* upstream skills are worth having and *why*, and [`../scripts/sync-third-party.py`](../scripts/sync-third-party.py) installs them from their own repos via the [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) CLI.

From the repo root:

```bash
./scripts/sync-third-party.py          # install everything below, at latest
./scripts/sync-third-party.py --check  # compare the manifest against what's installed
./scripts/sync-third-party.py --outdated  # list installed skills whose upstream folder changed since
./scripts/sync-third-party.py --list   # print the list with the reason for each
```

Re-running the sync re-fetches each skill, so **sync is also the upgrade command**. The flip side: there is no version pinning; every sync moves each skill to whatever is on its upstream default branch that day. Read the diff upstream before syncing if that matters.

A source that fails to install doesn't stop the rest: the sync carries on, links what's installed, then lists what failed and exits 1.

**Run the sync from a plain terminal, not from inside a coding-agent session.** The CLI detects the agent it's running under and installs to that agent alone, so a sync started inside Claude Code updates the store and Claude Code and silently leaves every other agent on its old copy.

A source can override the top-level `agents` list: `cloudflare/skills` is curated into five agents, while the other sources are curated into Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity.

The skills.sh CLI treats Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and Antigravity as "universal" agents: a global install writes only the store, `~/.agents/skills`, and never their own directories. So the sync links each curated skill into `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.copilot/skills`, `~/.gemini/skills` and `~/.gemini/config/skills` itself, for the agents its source lists. A real directory already sitting there is a stale copy from another channel; the sync refuses to replace it, and `--check` says so.

What `--check` reports. The first four rows mean the installs disagree with the manifest and make it exit 1; the rest only report, since another channel's install may be deliberate:

| | |
|---|---|
| `missing` / `conflict` | curated but not installed, or installed from a different repo than the manifest names |
| `drift` | an agent missed an update: its directory holds an older copy than the store, a universal agent is missing its link, or holds a stale copy instead of a link (move it aside, then sync) |
| `archived` | a skill the manifest has retired is still installed |
| `invocation` | the installed copy is user-invoked where `skills.json` says model-invoked, or the reverse: upstream flipped it, so update the entry's `invocation` and rebuild the catalog |
| `uncurated` | installed from a remote source but absent from the manifest |
| `unmanaged` | sitting in the store or an agent's directory with nothing managing it: another channel's install, or an upstream deletion left behind |
| `note` | store copies older than what the agents load. The CLI installs new skills straight into the agent directory and never refreshes an old `~/.agents/skills` entry, so these are leftovers, not a failed sync |

Curated skills are installed globally (`~/.agents/skills`), the same store the skills this repo owns land in, so a curated skill's name must never collide with one under [`skills/`](../skills/). The sync script refuses to run if it does.

To add one: find it (`npx skills find`), try it without installing (`npx skills use <owner/repo>@<skill>`), then add an entry to `skills.json` with a real reason and its `invocation` (`"user"` if its frontmatter sets `disable-model-invocation: true`, else `"model"`), and run `scripts/build-catalog.py`; the reason's first sentence becomes the line below.

## Curated skills

Generated from [`skills.json`](./skills.json) by `scripts/build-catalog.py`: each source's reason, each curated skill with the first sentence of its reason (`--list` prints them whole), grouped by its `invocation`, and the archived skills with theirs. An archived skill was curated once and retired, or considered and declined in favour of an owned skill; it stays in its source's `archived` list so the decision isn't re-litigated, the sync no longer installs it, and `--check` reports an `archived` line while a copy is still installed (`npx skills remove -g <name>` clears it). Re-curating one is moving its entry back from `archived` to `skills`.

### [cloudflare/skills](https://github.com/cloudflare/skills)

Cloudflare's own skills for the developer platform. Curated across every agent that already had them; see docs/adr/0003. The repo also ships commands/ and rules/, which only its Claude Code plugin installs; skipped deliberately. Pared to the four in use as of October 2026; the rest are archived. cloudflare and wrangler load only in Cloudflare Pages projects, so a month without loads isn't a reason to archive them.

#### Model-invoked

- **[cloudflare](https://github.com/cloudflare/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/cloudflare/SKILL.md)**: Umbrella platform skill: Workers, storage, AI, networking, security.
- **[wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/wrangler/SKILL.md)**: Correct CLI syntax for deploys and resource management.
- **[workers-best-practices](https://github.com/cloudflare/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/workers-best-practices/SKILL.md)**: Catches the Workers anti-patterns that bite in production: floating promises, global state, streaming, secrets.
- **[web-perf](https://github.com/cloudflare/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/web-perf/SKILL.md)**: Core Web Vitals and load analysis via Chrome DevTools MCP.

### [cloudflare/security-audit-skill](https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill)

Cloudflare's single-skill repo for security audits, the starting point of their vulnerability-discovery harness. Separate from cloudflare/skills. Its security bar (boundary and result, severity anchors) is also adapted into review-prs' Security lens, since diff reviews never load this skill.

#### Model-invoked

- **[security-audit](https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill/blob/HEAD/skills/security-audit/SKILL.md)**: Whole-codebase security audit: recon, parallel hunters, fresh verifiers that try to disprove each candidate, schema-checked findings.json and a report.

### [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)

The repo this one forked from. These are the skills worth tracking upstream rather than owning; see docs/adr/0009.

#### Model-invoked

- **[codebase-design](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/codebase-design/SKILL.md)**: Deep-module vocabulary.
- **[diagnosing-bugs](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)**: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions.
- **[domain-modeling](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/domain-modeling/SKILL.md)**: Maintains ubiquitous language (GLOSSARY.md) and ADRs.
- **[grilling](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/productivity/grilling/SKILL.md)**: The interview engine.
- **[research](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/research/SKILL.md)**: Delegates reading legwork to a background agent and lands findings as Markdown in the repo.
- **[tdd](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md)**: Red → green at agreed seams, with what a test worth keeping looks like.
- **[wizard](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/wizard/SKILL.md)**: Generates a bash wizard for steps only a human can do: dashboard clicks, secrets into .env and gh.

- **[code-review](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/code-review/SKILL.md)**: Replaced by the owned review-prs skill (docs/adr/0005), which keeps its Standards and Spec axes and smell baseline and adds the GitHub loop: find PRs with no real review, comment inline, fix, resolve. Its local fixed-point review is review-prs's local mode.
- **[pr](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/pr/SKILL.md)**: Replaced by the owned pr-body skill. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Replaced by the owned arch-review skill (docs/adr/0004), which adapts its scan and candidate format but writes the backlog into the repo and implements it. - **[grill-me](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md)**: Never invoked in chat history (Claude transcripts from 30 Aug, prompt history from May, Codex sessions Aug-Sep 2026). ### [caldoai/skills](https://github.com/caldoai/skills)

Two skills on agent-friendly codebases. Only prune-tests is curated; untangle-codebase's lens was adapted into the owned arch-review. The repo was a day old when curated (one commit, 17 November 2026) and syncs are unpinned, so read its diff before syncing.

#### Model-invoked

- **[prune-tests](https://github.com/caldoai/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/prune-tests/SKILL.md)**: Deletes or rewrites tests that guard no behavior: ones asserting removed code, ones that can't fail (testing the browser, the mock, the type system), and ones tied to the implementation; plus duplicates and production code that exists only for tests.

<details>
<summary>Archived (1)</summary>

- **[untangle-codebase](https://github.com/caldoai/skills/blob/HEAD/skills/untangle-codebase/SKILL.md)**: Never curated: a one-pass whole-codebase refactor that competes with the owned arch-review's backlog of stacked PRs. Its coupling lens (hidden links, needless links, surplus), special cases as evidence, git co-change and the comments rule were adapted into arch-review instead (MIT, credited in its CREDITS.md).
